reviews.review:
Currently, i'm in a very difficult spot for how I feel about the game. I think it nails the atmosphere tremendously well and feels like it could easily challenge phas for the horror game in my friend group. I think the ability to tweak how your investigator to be better with certain items and be worse in other regards is really cool. Being able to have the truck friend feel as effective as everyone else if they get scared easily is great. The relics you receive give minor buffs to using certain items. I've received one that increases the aoe of UV and a second for aoe of flashlight. 

Yet in this comparison, we must also look at the gameplay loops of the two games. I will preface this that I haven't been able to do any of the roguelite mechanics in this.
Both games focus on gathering evidence to figure out the ghost. The primary difference is that in NOX you also banish the ghost. In concept, this is easy and even with the 'punishments' for getting it wrong, its still process of elimination. 
The problem lies in evidence. In phas, you can remove evidence as you find or fail to find certain types. I am also aware that the spirit box is bugged right now so i'll put that to the side for now. The other evidence types are difficult to confirm. Motion camera feels iffy at best, emf being a perfect item in phas feels flawed here, ultraviolet is useful but hard to know where to check, recording feels the most consistent but i either have not received any confirmed ones or i'm incorrect in my guess, ghost writing also feels consistent but i will explain why that is concerning in a moment. 
I'm sure I missed one but the other thing phas does is that there is a room for the ghost to sit in. I think that's true here as well but i think its only visible when the ghost hunts.

speaking of hunts.... The ghost hunts in this game as well, starting with a loud musical sting. Well, let me rephrase from my experience. The ghost enters a seeking phase, looking for the player, upon seeing a player a musical sting activates then the hunt begins proper. The ghost then advances towards the player. If the player has a crucifix out, they burn over the course of around 5-10 seconds then (presumably) return to their starting location. Note: the ghost can still grab you if its not fully burned. After a few moments, couldn't get a time, the ghost returns to a dormant state. The hunt amounts increase as sanity burns. Simple, no? Well, lets look at a certain thing I said. It seeks, then when it sees you, the musical sting happens. So far, I have lost a life 3 times to turning a corner into the ghost and couldn't whip out that crucifix fast enough. You can burn your personal relic to prevent dying to the ghost but you only get those once a day or by finding the coins. 

Ah yes, coins. These give you bonus lives but there's 2 problems with them. You can find them naturally or by picking up the tabby on each map then placing it. The cat should point towards where the coins are but from my experience, much like a normal cat, it stares off in a direction. You also only receive these coins if you succeed at banishing the ghost. If you leave early, you don't receive them. Nothing wrong with that but the difficulty of the game means that its easier to learn what you can and leave. It still randomizes the area, reduces the free gear you get and reduces the money you receive. Makes sense for a roguelike. 

In addition to all of this, I'd like to talk about the dowsing stick. This is a small plumbob on a string that glows and (I think?) points in the area of cursed objects. Now, wendigo does say it can't make cursed objects. The problem for this is that the dowsing stick. Has. Physics. I can move 2 cm and it spins faster than an industry grade fan and that is with low bobbing on the character. Simple fix would be removing its physic and have it spin while its trying to find the cursed object before locking into a direction. I'm not a game programmer so I could just be mean on that for barely any reasons. 

Finally, lets talk about the sanity system. This is something I cross referenced with my friend who i'm going to duo in this with (and I currently duo with her in phas). There were times where both of us chill in the house for upwards of 5 minutes with minimal drain. Then we see or barely hear an event and drop to 60. There's also fuse boxes. Supposedly. Both of us played a total of 6 maps? and she only found it on a hotel type map. The beginner maps to learn how to play are old houses that seemingly don't have fuse boxes which means you can never turn on lights. Which means you have a constant sanity drain you can't deal with. Frustrating to say the least. 

Now, that's a lot of negatives and even to me, its a bit disheartening. I do see a lot of promise however. Things just need to be tweaked to be more consistent. Less physics on certain items, easier ways to tell if an item worked or not, guaranteed closets and fuse boxes on every map (like 1, please), maybe a practice house for ghost hunting proper with 5-7 rooms and helps you learn how to properly use the items in the field. I think this is legitmately one of the biggest contenders to fight against phas but more groundwork needs to be put in. As we get updates, I will be streaming it but at this moment, I cannot say that anyone should buy it. You should try it! If I could give a mixed review I would. Please don't consider this to be a hate message or a contrarian review. I would love to love this game but its hard
reviews.developer_response:
Thanks a ton for taking the time to write such a deep review. 

The backend team has been informed of this review to take a look and further develop the systems.

You’ve touched on several things already on our radar: 
- better evidence clarity
- more predictable sanity mechanics

We’re currently testing fixes for some of these systems and will keep the community updated as they roll out.

Thanks again for the review and we hope to continue to improve N.O.X. for you!
